goemotions_rl.note: First run invalidated by Qwen3 default enable_thinking=True (model rambled to the 64-token cap, reward ~0). Rerun with enable_thinking=False fixed it; see final_results.json.

findings: Base model for text RL matches Fireworks exactly: Qwen3-0.6B. Same dataset, same 64-token cap, same Jaccard reward — apples-to-apples.

Qwen3's chat template defaults to enable_thinking=True, which made the model fill the whole 64-token budget with <think> reasoning and score zero. Fix = --apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' (Fireworks runs this model with enable_thinking=False).

Miles (self-hosted GRPO, KL=0) reaches final Jaccard 0.60 vs Fireworks 0.34, and sampled micro-F1 ~0.44 vs 0.38 — but ends at 100% truncated responses, so the higher Jaccard is partly verbose-but-parseable output.
FSDP saves DCP (torch.distributed.checkpoint); export_hf is Megatron-only, so a held-out eval needs a DCP->HF loader.
